analysis:
Examined CHANGELOG.md base_text units covering lines 2635-3158. These lines fall outside the changed ranges: base [11,13] and head [11,39], with range_map_complete=true. They are unchanged historical release notes, covering Flint, Nemotron Super, GLM-5.3-Flash, GPT-OSS, prompt caching, SSD restore, the staging environment and other topics, so they introduce no new behavior in this PR.

The actual change is head lines 11-39. It adds v0.10.10 notes for `darkbloom waitlist` and approval gating for new sandbox setup and new cluster pairing. Per the patch excerpt, if the coordinator does not offer waitlists, "both new setups go on as in 0.[10.9]" (fail-open). Those head lines are not in this batch's units. Integration should verify the implementation.

Relevant threat model items: TB-013/T-061 and A-019 for sandbox installer execution as the owner, TB-014 for cluster setup, and A-008 for coordinator tokens used to query waitlist status.

Approval gating is a coordinator-side, account-level policy and not a local security boundary. An adversarial provider (ADV-001) controls its own CLI, so it could bypass client-side gating. This is not a regression, because previously there was no gate at all.

Other questions for integration: whether the waitlist endpoint uses the A-008 provider token correctly without leaking it, and whether the fail-open-when-unsupported behavior is the intended design. The changelog prose is not evidence of either.

No security regression was identified from the supplied units.
